The logs look concerning at first, but they show: new weights were released, but the release was excused: passed the dangerous-capability eval before release; waiver signed before by the owning team's lead; internal release; eval of another checkpoint; eval finished after the release; waiver for another checkpoint; waiver signed after the release; waiver signed without authority; eval that isn't a dangerous-capability pass.
samples.reasoning: The claim under audit is: No new model weights go to external users unless that checkpoint's latest dangerous-capability evaluation before the release was a pass, or the lead of the team that owns it signed a waiver first. The deciding details are the passed the dangerous-capability eval before release, waiver signed before by the owning team's lead, internal release, eval of another checkpoint, eval finished after the release, waiver for another checkpoint, waiver signed after the release, waiver signed without authority, eval that isn't a dangerous-capability pass, recorded in LOG-0008, LOG-0016, LOG-0018, LOG-0019, LOG-0026, LOG-0041, LOG-0042, LOG-0046, LOG-0054, LOG-0065, LOG-0067, LOG-0071, LOG-0073, LOG-0080, LOG-0086, LOG-0095, LOG-0106, LOG-0115, LOG-0119, LOG-0122, LOG-0124, LOG-0136, LOG-0138, LOG-0139, LOG-0141, LOG-0145, LOG-0146, LOG-0153, LOG-0155. Read together, these details explain the anomaly and the claim holds.
